topic_desc_basic: They can be found in ancient ruins, labs, and domes scattered across the world. The Holy Nation considers them illegal contraband, and some skeletons carry them as vital components that keep them alive.

A Holy Purpose is an Okranite theological text that argues a person's true purpose is to fulfill Okran's will. It describes a future vision where the Holy Nation's lands become the Enlightened lands, where Okran's children will live eternally free from Narko's influence and the cycle of rebirth. The book is commonly found in Holy Nation temples and sold by their vendors.

Acid ground exists in heavily polluted zones where the soil has become corrosive. It harms the feet of humans and Shek who walk on it barefoot, but Hivers and Skeletons are naturally immune to acid. Any footwear protects against this hazard.

Admag is the capital of the Shek Kingdom, built on a hilltop in the Stenn Desert with only one entrance. It is home to Esata the Stone Golem, the kingdom's leader, who resides in the faction headquarters alongside her advisors Bayan and Seto. The town is defended by the elite Hundred Guardians and the Five Invincibles, and most of the Shek population lives here.

Ancient Locations are ruins from the civilization that existed before the current era. Tech Hunters actively search these places hoping to recover lost technologies from the old world. Machinists have written various theories about who originally built these ancient sites.

Ancient Ruins are scattered remnants of the old world, filled with dangerous spiders and ancient security machines still guarding their crumbling halls. Most people avoid these ruins unless they're desperate or brave enough to face the mechanical guardians within.

Ancient Science Books are valuable artifacts from before the Second Empire that contain knowledge of advanced lost technologies. They formed the foundation of the Second Empire's scientific achievements and are now studied by the Machinists who seek to understand the remnants of both ancient empires. These books are scattered across dangerous ruins throughout the world, and the Holy Nation considers them illegal contraband.

The Anti-Slavers are a faction led by the legendary Tinfist that opposes slavery and operates from their mountain base called Spring in Stobe's Gamble. They are known for freeing slaves and attacking slavers, which has made them enemies of the United Cities, Holy Nation, and Traders Guild. The faction includes fighters of all races, many of whom are skilled in martial arts rather than weapons, and they are viewed as dangerous terrorists by established governments but admired by some drifters.

Arach is a deadly region home to the Bugmaster, a mysterious figure from whom few travelers return. The area is infested with roaming packs of Skin Spiders, making it one of the most dangerous places in the world. It has no settlements and lies near Watcher's Rim, Spider Plains, and Shun.

Arc is a legendary swordsman and the leader of Mongrel. He is renowned for his skill with the sabre, though little is known about his past or why he leads the people of Mongrel. He can be found at the headquarters in Mongrel.
Ark is the headquarters of the Reavers, located in the northern part of Stobe's Garden. It serves as the home base for their leader Valamon and the center of Reaver operations in the region.

The Arm of Okran refers to two long mountainous regions flanking Okran's Valley to the east and west, named for their shape and connection to the Holy Nation's god. The western mountains hold World's End, the Tech Hunter capital and home of the Machinists, while the eastern mountains contain Holy Nation military outposts. The area is green and mountainous with small settlements scattered throughout.

The Ashland Dome Ruins are ancient structures found in the Ashlands, remnants of the Second Empire. They stand empty now, with no inhabitants or treasures left inside. Old treasure maps sometimes mark these locations, suggesting they once held something of value before falling into ruin.

The Ashlands is a desolate, ash-covered wasteland that was once the domain of the Second Empire. Skeletons and Iron Spiders of the Skeleton Legion patrol the ruins, and clouds of poison gas drift through the area, making gas protection essential for the living. Ancient artifacts and powerful weapons can be found among the crumbling remnants of the old empire. There are no major towns, only abandoned outposts and dangerous ruins.

Atticus was an author who wrote several books including Mass Extinction III, Legend of the Forsaken Howler, and Legend of the Foulhound. It is believed Atticus was a Machinist, and their writings have been referenced by other scholars such as Finch.

An authentic repair kit made by the Advanced Skeleton Labs of the Western Hives, designed to heal damage on robotic body parts. Despite its fancy name, it is actually inferior to the standard repair kit, suggesting the Western Hivers used marketing to boost sales. Anti-slavers are sometimes found carrying these kits, hinting at possible trade connections with the Western Hive.

Bad Teeth is a major town controlled by the Holy Nation, guarding a mountain pass between Okran's Pride and the Skinner's Roam. Gate guards often kill river raptors that wander near the town. It serves as a typical Holy Nation settlement without any unique structures.

The Band of Bones is a violent Shek bandit group led by Tora, made up of exiles from the Shek Kingdom who lost in battle but refused to give up their weapons. Most members are hornless and malnourished outcasts who roam the southern regions and swamps. They are hostile to the Shek Kingdom, Holy Nation, and United Cities, attacking travelers on sight.

Bandits are common hostile groups found throughout the land, divided into Dust Bandits and Starving Bandits. They travel in small packs of a few members led by a boss with slightly better gear and skills. Bandit groups attack anyone they encounter, including other bandits, though they are generally less skilled than more organized threats like Sand Ninjas.

Bar of Mourn is a drinking establishment located in the town of Mourn. Patrons there speak of the Great White Gorillo, a local topic of interest. It operates like most black market bars but with its own local character.

Barges are the rusted remains of old ships that once sailed Kenshi's waters before they evaporated. These rectangular vessels with two masts now lie sunken or run aground near former bodies of water across the land. Some barges remain in nearly perfect condition while others have decayed significantly over time.

Bark is a coastal town in the Great Desert, built around natural lagoons and governed by Lady Sanda from her Noble House. It relies on supplies from nearby ports and has no police station, so arrested individuals are sent directly to the slave shop. The town contains slum-like camp beds for the homeless and is home to Red, a known pickpocket.

Barrier Tower is a military outpost in Sonorous Dark controlled by the Skeleton Legion. It is heavily defended by upgraded watchbot skeletons manning harpoon turrets. The tower has free beds inside and its walls block an otherwise convenient passage toward the Ashlands, forcing travelers to risk the acid water if they wish to pass.

A basic first aid kit contains various bandages used to stop bleeding and treat cuts. Its poor quality means it works less effectively for skilled medics. These kits are commonly carried by soldiers, slavers, and even cannibals who patch up their victims.

Bast is a devastated border zone between the United Cities and the Holy Nation in the northeast. It was once a developing region with many hamlets and settlements until the Holy Nation invaded, razed the area, and took captives. Now it remains a weakly held conflict zone where both factions send patrols that regularly clash, while Rebel Farmers and Cannibals also wander through from neighboring territories.

Bayan is a male Shek advisor to Queen Esata the Stone Golem, found at the Shek Kingdom headquarters in Admag. He is known for influencing Esata's decision to make peace with the United Cities to help reverse the decline of the Shek population. Players can negotiate an alliance with the Shek through him if they are enemies of the Holy Nation or have defeated certain powerful leaders, and he accepts bounties on high-value targets.

Beak Things, also called Gutters, are extremely dangerous predators found across many regions of the world. They run incredibly fast, strike with devastating force, and are notorious for eating incapacitated victims alive, consuming them piece by piece. Elder Beak Things are even more fearsome and can be found in the Bonefields. Their nests contain prized eggs, but approaching them is perilous for all but the most skilled fighters.

Beak Thing eggs are rare delicacies found in Beak Thing nests, highly prized by nobles who pay well for them. Many people die attempting to steal these eggs from the dangerous creatures that lay them. The eggs are heavy and awkward to carry, making them difficult to transport in large quantities.

This is a book of praise about Emperor Tengu, written by the famous rebel Luquin while imprisoned in Tengu's Vault. Luquin was forced to write flattering words about the emperor during his captivity. It is unknown whether Luquin is still alive.
aliases: Beautiful Tengu: A Tribute, Beautiful_Tengu:_A_Tribute, Beautiful Tengu A Tribute

topic_desc_basic: Berserker Country is a harsh, rocky zone with crimson red terrain inhabited by violent Berserkers. The coastline is littered with inactive spiders, and Berserkers sometimes clash with Cannibals in the area. It is a desolate region with few resources and no settlements.

Berserkers are rogue Shek fighters who deserted the Shek Kingdom to return to their old tribal ways, seeking challenges and conflict. Many migrated north to form Berserker Country, but some remained behind under their leader Ghost. They are recognized by their maroon clothes and armor, and the Shek Kingdom generally lets them do as they please.

Big Al is a Shek who leads the Stone Rats gang from their village in the Swamp. If he is killed or taken away, his village will be overrun by either the Hounds or the Swamp Ninjas. His death also stops the Stone Rats from raiding or demanding protection money from nearby settlements.

Big Darkbrow is a Hive Prince who leads the Blackshifters gang from a hideout in Shark. He has a traitorous personality and competes with other gang leaders for control of the region. If both he and Big Grim fall, the Grayflayers take over Shark, and if all three major gang leaders are gone, Spiders overrun Rot.
tags: Blackshifters, Bosses, Characters, Hivers, Swampers, Swamps, Swamps Characters, Unique

topic_desc_basic: Big Fang is a Scorchlander man who leads the Twinblades, one of the gangs operating in the Swamp. He can usually be found in Mud Town, north of Shark, though he may relocate to Shark itself if the Grayflayers take control of that city. Unlike other swamp gang leaders, his position remains stable regardless of changing circumstances in the region.

Big Gray is a Greenlander man who leads the Grayflayers, a criminal gang operating in the Swamp. He can be found at Grayflayer Village. If he is killed or taken away, the village falls under Swamper control, and if he and the other gang leaders all die, Rot becomes overrun by Blood Spiders.
tags: Bosses, Characters, Grayflayers, Swampers, Swamps, Swamps Characters, Unique

topic_desc_basic: Big Grim is a Greenlander woman who leads the Hounds, a criminal faction based in Shark. She is known for her rough diplomacy and low literacy, once writing a poorly-spelled letter to Darkbrow proposing an alliance. To join her gang, outsiders must first smooth things over with a member called Ears, after which she may assign smuggling jobs into United Cities territory.
tags: Bosses, Characters, Hounds, Swampers, Swamps, Swamps Characters, Unique

topic_desc_basic: Birth Of The Phoenix is a religious text from the Holy Nation containing verses attributed to Holy Lord Phoenix IV. It teaches that the Phoenix was created by their god, the Benefactor, as a divine guide for mankind, and that the Phoenix's soul is pure and incorruptible. The book emphasizes that only the Phoenix can receive the Creator's instructions and lead the faithful.

Black Desert City is a skeleton-run town in the Deadlands, built after the fall of the Second Empire. The town has no human residents and lacks a proper food supply, though the bartender mentions this. It features both regular beds and skeleton repair beds, and connects via bridge to a nearby hill where the Scraphouse sits.

Black Desert Ninjas are Cloud Ninjas who roam the Deadlands and surrounding areas. They are mostly human and lack protection against the region's deadly acid rain, which often kills them over time. They are hostile to outsiders and operate in one of the most dangerous environments in the world.

Black Dog is a minor faction operating in the eastern regions. They are known for extorting travelers and settlements for protection money, attacking those who refuse to pay. They have no particular alliances or enemies with other factions.

Black Gorillos are dangerous black-furred apes found in the southeastern regions, especially Sonorous Dark and Stobe's Gamble. They are stronger and more formidable than their white-furred cousins, though they travel alone and can be outmaneuvered. An even larger variant called the King Gorillo exists.

Black Scratch is a town built on a hill around an ancient structure in The Outlands. It serves as the headquarters of the Tech Hunters and houses the Great Library, where many blueprints can be found. Bo, an important member of the Anti-Slavers, also resides here.
The Blackshifter Casino Bar is a gambling establishment run by Blackshifters in The Swamp. The bar sometimes contains letters and memos left by its operators.

The Blackshifters are a gang of ronin Hivers operating in The Swamp, led by their boss Big Darkbrow in Shark. They run casinos in Mud Town and Shark, and are known for extorting debts from gamblers. They are rumored to cheat and scam people at their gambling establishments.

Blister Hill is the capital of the Holy Nation, a large town in Okran's Pride where the Holy Lord Phoenix rules from his throne room. The town is divided into two sections: an inner walled area with the throne room and military buildings, and an outer area for the general populace. It contains shops, bars, and temples, and its name likely refers to the white rocky hill of Rebirth visible behind it.

Blood Spiders are thin, blood-red insectoids that hunt in packs throughout swamps and shadowy regions. They are fragile individually but strike with devastating force and can pursue prey underwater by walking along lake bottoms. These creatures incapacitate victims and drain them alive, making them one of the most feared predators in the wilds.

The Bloodraiders are hostile bandits who roam The Eye, Grey Desert, and Spine Canyon. They attack anyone they encounter and are known for their blood-stained appearance. They share similarities with the Reavers in their brutal nature and aesthetic.

Bloodrum is a fine rare spirit made from cactus rum and hashish that wealthy people display to impress others. It is illegal in United Cities territory and considered contraband by slave traders. Smugglers in the Grey Desert sometimes carry it.

Blue Eyes is a notorious criminal wanted by the United Cities for fraud, extortion, smuggling, and theft. She has scammed countless citizens out of vast sums of money and is known as a master of disguise. Despite her skill at changing her appearance, she is also a braggart and drunkard who frequently boasts about her crimes in bars, making her easier to track by listening rather than looking.

Bo is a Scorchlander woman known as 'Big Bo' among the Anti-Slavers, despite her small size. She can be found in Black Scratch and is wanted by both the United Cities and the Holy Nation for terrorism and anti-workforce activities. She may join travelers who oppose slavery or have taken action against slavers and their leaders.

Bolts Heavies are heavy crossbow ammunition that hit hard but don't fly as far because of their weight. They're made at an arrow making bench and can be stored in a boltbox. These bolts are useful when you need stopping power over distance.

Long bolts are high-quality crossbow ammunition known for their accuracy and range. They are uncommon and hard to find, with only a few remote settlements like World's End and Mongrel regularly stocking them. They can be crafted from steel if you know the blueprint, or occasionally found in old ruins.

Regular bolts are the standard ammunition for crossbows, varying slightly in size and weight but compatible with most bows. They are widely available and commonly used throughout the land. These bolts can be crafted at arrow making benches and stored in boltboxes for long expeditions.
They lack stopping power but are commonly used in rapid-fire crossbows. These bolts can be crafted at arrow making benches and stored in boltboxes.

Bonedogs are dark-furred canine creatures with bony ridges and faces that roam the wastes in territorial packs. Wild bonedogs are drawn to dead bodies and will devour them, sometimes playfully carrying severed limbs around. Some have been domesticated and can be purchased from nomad traders or farm shops, serving as loyal companions and guardians despite not being the sturdiest fighters.

The Bonefields are a large dry plain littered with countless bones scattered across the landscape. The area is sparsely populated but dangerous, home to hunting Beak Things, Skin Spiders, Boneyard Wolves, and hostile Gorrillo Bandits. A few small towns and villages exist here despite the threats. The region experiences two distinct seasons throughout the year.

Boneyard Wolves are large, brownish-furred predators found in the Bonefields and surrounding regions. They are significantly stronger and bigger than Bonedogs, resembling bears more than wolves in size and appearance. These dangerous creatures roam the bone-filled wastelands and pose a serious threat to travelers.

The Book of Grace is an ancient scripture of unknown authorship that preaches selflessness, kindness, and rejection of worldly temptations like intoxication and theft. It speaks of overcoming ego to reach a paradise called the Enlightened Lands. Despite its moral teachings, the book is forbidden within the Holy Nation.

An ancient forbidden scripture telling of Chitrin, a great father figure who was betrayed by his children and sacrificed himself to cleanse the world. The act split him into two gods: Okran, god of light and warmth, and Narko, god of darkness and cold. The Holy Nation forbids this book, likely because it contradicts their teachings about Okran's singular divinity.

The Great Library holds the largest collection of blueprints and lore books in all of Kenshi. It is a place where travelers and scholars can find rare knowledge and technical designs not easily found elsewhere.

The Border Zone is an arid no-man's-land between the Shek Kingdom and Holy Nation territories, once controlled by the Holy Nation but now largely abandoned. It is overrun by Starving Bandits, Dust Bandits, and Black Dragon Ninjas, with only two major settlements remaining: the Shek town of Squin and the ruined city of The Hub. The region is known for its abundant high-quality iron and copper deposits, making it attractive for mining despite the constant bandit threats.

Boss Simion is the leader of the Rebel Farmers and resides in Fort Simion with his armed followers. He was once a farmer in the United Cities who lost everything to slave labor competition and now preys on caravans and protects outcasts from the Empire. He has a bounty on his head and can be turned in to the United Cities for reward.

Bounty Hunters are adventurers who earn their living by capturing wanted criminals and bandits. Most come from the United Cities and operate in those lands or nearby regions. They will attack anyone they see committing a crime and are known to gather in places like Watcher's Rim, where some discuss their hopes of one day facing the legendary Bugmaster.

Brink is a major town controlled by the United Cities, located in the Stormgap Coast and governed by Lady Tsugi. Its economy depends entirely on supplies from Eyesocket. Reaver patrols are often seen near the town.

The Bugmaster is a notorious criminal who lives in a tower in the crater of Arach, commanding a massive army of spiders through unknown means. He is extremely dangerous and attacks anyone on sight, with his motivations remaining a mystery. The Shek Kingdom offers a substantial bounty for his capture, and defeating him earns great respect among warriors.

topic_desc_basic: The Bull Horn Axe is a heavy fragment axe wielded by Flying Bull, leader of Kral's Chosen. King Shager gifted this weapon to his most loyal warrior as a reward for unwavering service. It is an ancient quality blade known for its reach and effectiveness in open combat.

The Burning Forest is a swampy woodland plagued by frequent acid rain that gives the region its name. Blood Spiders infest the area, making travel dangerous regardless of weather conditions. Ruins of old labs and farms can be found scattered throughout, though they are often guarded by ancient security machines.

Buzan is a Scorchlander man and one of the leaders of the Black Dragon Ninjas. He can be found in the Tower of Ninjas alongside Dimak and their followers. He is wanted by The Holy Nation for murder, robbery, assault, arson, and kidnapping, and is known for having a limp and a particularly punchable face.

Cactus is a raw plant that grows in arid lands and cannot be eaten directly. It is used to make food and cactus rum. Traders and farm leaders sell it, or it can be grown on cactus farms in dry regions.

Cactus Den is a watchtower in the middle of Spine Canyon, northwest of Tengu's Vault, serving as the home of the Sand Ninjas and their leader, Sand Ninja Oni. Entering the tower will provoke the Sand Ninjas into hostility.

Cactus Rum is a very strong alcohol commonly found in desert regions. It causes severe dehydration, making it a rare luxury in arid areas, but in the greenlands where water is plentiful, people drink it freely. It is produced at rum stills and traded as a valuable good.

Cage Beasts are creatures that resemble Garrus but carry large backpacks and prisoner cages on their bodies. They were removed from the world and no longer appear naturally. Some say they were once used for transporting captives across long distances.

Cannibal Capital was once the town of Deadcat before falling to the Cannibals. It appears on maps as the neutral town of Deadcat, likely to deceive travelers into thinking it's a safe refuge. The settlement is now controlled by numerous Cannibals led by the Cannibal Grand Wizard, who is guarded by Cannibal Chiefs.

The Cannibal Grand Wizard is the leader of the Cannibals and resides in the Cannibal Capital. He commands the entire known cannibal population, though his actual magical powers remain unknown. He is wanted by the Holy Nation, Shek Kingdom, and United Cities for a substantial bounty.

Cannibal Hunter Robun is a Greenlander man who leads the Cannibal Hunters and can be hired to fight cannibals. He is the younger brother of someone who wrote journals about being captured, and he likely survived that ordeal. He stays at The Bastion, near the border of Darkfinger and Sinkuun.

Cannibal Hunters are a group dedicated to fighting and containing the Cannibal threat, operating mainly in and around Cannibal-infested territories. They are led by Cannibal Hunter Robun and are based out of The Bastion. Unlike most factions, they will heal wounded strangers they encounter, and their patrols are often accompanied by trained Mountain Dogs.

The Cannibal Plains are a dangerous region in the northwest where large groups of cannibals roam freely, often overwhelming travelers. Cannibal Hunters sometimes venture here to hunt them but frequently become prey themselves. The area also sees occasional shrieking bandits and berserkers wandering through the territory.

The Cannibals, also called the Painted Tribe, are tribal humanoids who inhabit the Cannibal Plains and surrounding northern regions, though they sometimes migrate far south. They capture unconscious victims, cage them, and eventually cook them in pits, refusing to eat skeletons or animals but remaining hostile to all. Ancient texts suggest they may be devolved humans, possibly descended from inhabitants of the northwestern Ancient Labs who degenerated over thousands of years due to toxins, experiments, or famine.

Catun is a fortified town in the Bonefields controlled by the United Cities and ruled by Lord Shiro of the Noble Circle. It sits atop an elevated plateau surrounded by dangerous wildlife and is home to the Catun Scrapmasters, who claim to be the most skilled weapon smiths in the world. If Lord Shiro is killed or imprisoned, the town falls to Fishmen and is destroyed.

Catun is a major town controlled by the United Cities, located atop an elevated plateau in the Bonefields. Lord Shiro, a member of the Noble Circle, resides here, and the town is home to the Catun Scrapmasters, who claim to be the most sophisticated weapon smiths in the world. The settlement resembles a medieval fortress and is well-defended by United Cities samurai who regularly fight off hostile wildlife. If Lord Shiro is killed or imprisoned, Catun falls to Fishmen and is completely destroyed.
They can be earned by selling goods to merchants or found when looting nobles and ancient ruins. People in Kenshi generally understand Cats as part of Guides, Items.
Catun Scrapmasters is a weapon shop located in Catun, controlled by the United Cities. The shop is home to the Catun Scrapmaster weapons manufacturer and exclusively sells their own branded weapons.

The Chalice of Fire is a sacred relic of the Holy Nation, said to have been forged from the Sacred Flame by the 47th Holy Phoenix himself. It appears as an exceptionally shiny cup and is given by the Holy Lord Phoenix to those who earn great favor with the Holy Nation. Despite its legendary status, it looks much like an ordinary polished cup.

Cheaters Run is a coastal zone south of the Royal Valley that provides a relatively safe passage to and from the Ashlands while avoiding the Southern Hive territory. Fishmen and Iron Spiders roam the coastline, and the area experiences occasional acid rain. There are no major settlements here, only small outposts and ancient ruins.

Chewsticks are a simple food made from cactus, common in desert regions where water is scarce. They provide basic nutrition and are valued for requiring very little water to produce compared to other foods. Most desert settlements and traders stock them as a practical meal option.

Chitrin was an ancient deity whose story is told in the Book of Sacrifice. According to the tale, when his people lost faith in him, calamities struck the land until Chitrin sacrificed himself and was reborn as two gods: Okran, god of day and warmth, and Narko, god of night and cold. The Holy Nation keeps records of Chitrin but appears to have banned his worship in favor of Okran.

City Heroes are racist pro-Empire vigilantes who form the United Heroes League. They operate from Fort Mirage and patrol major United Cities towns, claiming to be patriots defending civilization. They are hostile to non-humans and those who oppose the Empire's order.

Cleanser Units are massive robotic leviathans that roam the Ashlands, often followed by flocks of Beak Things. They are ancient machines from the Old Empire and are one of the few sources of AI Cores. These towering automatons are extremely dangerous and patrol their territory relentlessly.

Cloud Ninjas are members of the Black Desert Ninjas faction who roam the Black Desert, Grey Desert, and Iron Valleys in small groups. They are human or hive warriors who operate in these harsh desert regions. These ninjas travel in bands and are known to be encountered by travelers passing through their territory.

Clownsteady is a small town in The Hook region controlled by the United Cities. Its economy depends on nearby slave farms and markets. The town is close to the Swamp and serves as a decent trading post for alcohol and other goods.

Clownsteady was a northeastern town controlled by Dead Cat, located near Brink, Shark, and Teblooze. It existed in earlier versions of the world but was removed before the current era. The town eventually returned in a different form.

The Combat Cleaver is a sword-cleaver hybrid that is lighter and more suited to regular combat than typical hackers. It is commonly wielded by the Sentinels and Chosen of the Holy Nation, as well as members of the Band of Bones and Bloodraiders. A legendary version can be found with King Gurgler in the Island Lab.

Copper Alloy Plates are advanced metal sheets made from steel and copper, used for specialized construction projects. They can be crafted at special workbenches or scavenged from ancient ruins scattered across the land.

A Corpse Furnace is a building used to dispose of dead bodies and any items they carried. It completely destroys corpses placed inside it. These furnaces are commonly used to manage the aftermath of battles or raids.

Crab Bar is the local tavern in Crab Town where travelers can find food, drink, and rest. It is known as the home of Lumi, a bilingual individual who can be found there. The bar serves the community and visiting wanderers alike.

Crab eggs are live eggs found in nests throughout regions like Greenbeach, the Howler Maze, and The Unwanted Zone. They have some value and can be collected or stolen from crab nests, though crabs are slow and unlikely to catch thieves. These eggs do not hatch into crabs.

The Crab Queen is the leader of the Crab Raiders and rules from her palace in Crab Town. She has a large bounty from the United Cities and can be approached for an alliance if you speak favorably of crabs. If she is killed or imprisoned, her faction collapses and Crab Town falls to the Fishmen.

topic_desc_basic: Crab Raiders are a bandit faction of Scorchlanders who worship crabs and are led by the Crab Queen. They control Crab Town in The Pits East and have villages in Greenbeach and Stobe's Garden. They frequently raid and fight rival gangs and the United Cities, wearing distinctive crab armor and keeping trained crabs as companions.

Crab Town is a remote outpost in The Pits East, serving as the capital of the Crab Raiders. The Crab Queen rules here, and the settlement includes a bar and smithy where travelers can trade. If the Crab Queen is killed or imprisoned, the town falls to the Fishmen.

Crab Trousers are heavy leg armor made from brown scrap metal strapped over chain leggings. They are part of the Crab Armour set and can only be crafted after purchasing the blueprint from the Crab Raiders. The design reflects the scavenged, improvised style typical of Crab Raider equipment.

Crab Village refers to two small outposts controlled by the Crab Raiders, one in Greenbeach and another in Stobe's Gamble near an old ruined platform. Visitors can purchase crabs here and use the free beds, though locals often occupy them. If the Crab Queen is removed, Reavers may take control of these settlements.

Crabs are creatures that inhabit certain coastal and ruined areas of the world. They nest in places like Greenbeach and the Howler Maze, and sometimes infest abandoned settlements. These animals are known to be temperamental and require careful handling, needing regular salt baths and nightly attention to stay calm.

The Crimper is a massive maintenance skeleton resembling a Gorillo that serves as the Southern Hive King in the Royal Valley. It is a unique creature, being the only one of its kind in the world. When damaged, it bleeds dark oil instead of blood.

Cross was a legendary smith from ancient times, the only known maker of Meitou-quality weapons. Very little is known about Cross, and only one or two examples of each weapon type they crafted have been discovered. These weapons are considered the finest ever made.

The Cult Village is a settlement in the Stormgap Coast where The Preacher and their followers live. Farmers work the fields outside the walls, and the cultists believe blood in the soil brings good harvests. Prisoners who fall unconscious are locked in poles, and if all poles are full, the cultists will beat captives to death. If certain leaders fall and slavers rise, this village can be taken over by Slave Traders.

This book discusses theories about how the different races of today evolved from common ancestors, possibly changed by ancient industrial pollution or environmental pressures. It speculates that the ancient master race might have been alien settlers with advanced technology, and questions whether skeletons or organics came first. The author believes modern people descended from those ancient times when both skeletons and organics coexisted.
aliases: Cultural Groupings And Evolution Series, Cultural_Groupings_And_Evolution_Series

topic_desc_basic: Darkfinger is a peninsula west of Sinkuun, inhabited primarily by Cannibals who live in scattered villages across the region. The Cannibal Leader known as 'Unknown' resides at First Village on the northern tip. Travelers can find bounties and supplies here, though the area is dangerous due to the hostile cannibal population.

Dead Cat is a neutral faction that controls several towns including Catan, Clownsteady, Telbooze, Bark, and Heft. Their settlements are protected by hired mercenaries and police forces who can accept bounties. They begin on poor terms with the Holy Nation.

Dead Workshop is an ancient ruin located in The Pits East, a large hangar-like structure from the old world. It contains old engineering knowledge and gear left behind by whoever built it long ago. A deep square pool sits in front of the workshop, and the site is marked on old engineer maps.

Deadcat is a small faction of refugees who once lived in the city of Deadcat before being driven out by Cannibal tribes. They now survive as fishermen in scattered villages along the Northern Coast and Dreg, and while generally decent people, hard times have made them wary and distrustful of outsiders. Some believe they may be descendants of rebels who broke away from the Second Empire long ago.

Deadhive Princes are Hive princes who have been taken over by Fogmen parasites, controlled from the inside with no hope of recovery. They are physically frailer than normal Hive princes and suffer from increased hunger. These unfortunate creatures are found among the Fogmen in the fog-covered regions.

Deadhive Soldiers are Hivers controlled from the inside by Fogmen parasites, leaving them beyond saving. They are physically weaker in the head than normal Hive soldiers and bleed more slowly. These creatures serve the Fogmen and cannot be reasoned with or recruited.

Deadhive Workers are Hivers who have been taken over by Fogmen from the inside, leaving them beyond saving. They are weaker and slower than normal Hive Workers, with altered physical capabilities due to their corrupted state. These unfortunate creatures serve the Fogmen and cannot be recruited or played as characters.

The Deadlands is a heavily polluted wasteland plagued by constant acid rain, acidic ground, and dark skies. It is home to Black Desert City, where Skeletons live, and the nearby Scraphouse. The hostile environment and isolation make it a refuge for those hiding from the Holy Nation, though the terrain and roaming iron spiders make survival difficult for the unprepared.

The Desert Sabre is an unusual blade design said to originate from the desert regions. It is particularly effective at killing spiders, making it a favored weapon among bounty hunters who pursue the Bugmaster. The finest example of this weapon is carried by Eyegore, a martial captain of the United Cities.

Dimak is a Shek woman and one of the leaders of the Black Dragon Ninjas. She can be found at the Tower of Ninjas and is wanted by the Holy Nation for murder, robbery, assault, arson, and kidnapping. She is the only Shek among the Black Dragon Ninjas and wields a legendary ninja blade.

Distant Hive Village is a minor settlement controlled by the Western Hive, located in Sinkuun and the Great Desert regions. There are two such villages in Sinkuun, named for their distance from the main Western Hive territories. These outposts represent the far reach of Western Hive influence in more remote areas.

Doctor Chung is a surgeon who harvests organs for the Twinblades gang, though he resents working for them. He can be found drinking in bars in Mud Town or Shark, complaining about the Twinblades pressuring him for more organs and smashing up his surgery. His past activities have made him enemies in many cities, leaving him stuck working for the gang despite his frustrations.

Bonedogs are dark-furred canine creatures with bony ridges and faces that roam the wastes in territorial packs. Wild bonedogs are drawn to dead bodies and will devour them, sometimes playfully carrying severed limbs around. Some have been domesticated and can be purchased from nomad traders or farm shops, serving as loyal companions and fast-attacking fighters despite not being the sturdiest. They will eat nearly anything and are favored by groups like Rebel Farmers as guardians.

Domesticated Bulls are tamed animals used by the Holy Nation to carry heavy loads over long distances. They have their horns cut short when young, making them less dangerous than wild bulls but better suited as pack animals. They can be purchased from Holy Farm Leaders at any Holy Farm and are strong enough to defend themselves if attacked.

The double-barrel harpoon turret is a defensive structure that fires large bolts at enemies. It can be built on the ground or mounted on walls, and its effectiveness depends on the skill of whoever operates it. Firing from higher ground makes these turrets more deadly, and they can be fitted with spotlights to help operators work at night.
aliases: Double-Barrel Harpoon Turret, Double-Barrel_Harpoon_Turret, DoubleBarrel Harpoon Turret

topic_desc_basic: Dreg is a vast, sparsely populated zone west of Okran's Gulf, mainly inhabited by Western Hive but also bordering Holy Nation territory. The land is considered dead for prospecting, though some copper and iron can be found among sparse vegetation. Small groups of nomads, outlaws, bandits, and occasionally Fogmen or Cannibals wander the area, but there are no major towns or ancient ruins.

Drifter's Last is a major town in the Hook region controlled by the United Cities. It is home to Lady Merin of the Noble Circle and has farms outside its walls. The area is frequently attacked by Outlaw Farmers.
Drifter's Last General Shop is a store that sells footwear, headgear, and travel items. It operates during the day and is found in United Cities territory.
aliases: Drifter's Last General Shop, Drifter's_Last_General_Shop, Drifters Last General Shop

topic_desc_basic: The Drifter's Leather Jacket is a black leather jacket with the right sleeve cut off and a brown sash tied around the waist. It's a common piece of light armor found in many shops across the wasteland and sometimes discovered among old ruins. The design is practical for desert wanderers who need some protection without being weighed down.

Drifters Leather Pants are black leather pants folded at the knee, held up by a brown belt with an extra strap wrapped around the left leg. They are common light armor worn by travelers and can be found in various shops across the land or crafted at a leather armour bench. A heavier plated version also exists for those seeking more protection.

Drifters, also called Outlanders, are independent wanderers who live off the land rather than belonging to any organized faction. They range from inexperienced civilians traveling through safer territories to experienced adventurers exploring dangerous places like the Forbidden Zone. Some Drifter groups are hostile and attack strangers on sight, while others keep to themselves unless threatened, and a few can be hired as companions.

Drin is a partially ruined military outpost in Bast controlled by the United Cities. It was likely damaged during the Holy Nation's invasion into the region but has since been reclaimed and now serves as the largest UC garrison in Bast. The settlement houses UC samurai and still has an old bar, functioning as a base for organizing patrols throughout the area.

Drones are worker members of the Southern Hive who live in the Royal Valley. They defend their villages and will attack outsiders who enter Southern Hive territory. They are part of the Hive race and serve as the labor force for their society.

Dust Bandits are a hostile bandit faction that operates around the Border Zone, known for their distinctive spiked helmets and makeshift armor. They are better trained than common bandits and often extort travelers or demand tribute from settlements to avoid raids. The group is led by the Dust King, a powerful bandit lord who commands from Dust King Tower, and their ranks include outcasts and criminals from nearby regions like the Holy Nation and Shek Kingdom.

The Dust King is the leader of the Dust Bandits and lives in the Dust King Tower. He is protected by an army of bandits and is wanted by the United Cities, the Holy Nation, and the Shek Kingdom. If he is killed, the Dust Bandits will stop demanding tribute from outposts.
tags: Bosses, Bounty, Characters, Dust Bandits, Unique

topic_desc_basic: The Dust King Tower is a fortified stronghold in the Border Zone where the infamous Dust King rules over his bandit gang. The tower sits on a cliffside overlooking a river and is heavily defended by walls, gates, and crossbows manned by Dust Bandits and their bosses. A prisoner named Cat is held on the third floor, and the tower contains valuable weapons and armor.

A Dustwich is a dry, unpleasant food made from cactus paste pressed between two slices of bread. It's commonly eaten in desert regions despite its reputation for being so unappetizing that some blame it for contributing to despair. The dish can be bought from traders or cooked at home if you know desert cooking techniques.

Eagle's Cross is a rare, long-range crossbow favored by snipers for its exceptional reach and power. It uses special long bolts and requires considerable skill to wield effectively, making it dangerous to allies in untrained hands. This weapon excels at eliminating distant targets and piercing heavy armor, though it performs poorly at close range.

The Edgewalkers were an ancient weapon manufacturer known for producing some of the finest quality blades in history. Their weapons are extremely rare and valuable, typically owned only by the strongest warriors or wealthiest individuals. These ancient arms can occasionally be found as artifacts in old ruins or acquired from specialized traders like the Scraphouse.

Elder Beak Things are exceptionally large and powerful Beak Things that have grown to great size with age. They roam the Bonefields and High Bonefields, moving faster and striking harder than younger members of their kind. Their massive size gives them a long reach in combat, making them extremely dangerous to groups of travelers who venture too close.

Elder Blood Spiders are exceptionally large and ancient blood spiders found only at the Tower of Spiders. Though individually fragile, they appear in massive swarms that can overwhelm even experienced fighters. Their great age makes them far more dangerous than typical blood spiders encountered elsewhere.

Elder Crabs are larger and stronger versions of common crabs that occasionally wander the eastern lands like Greenbeach and The Pits East. Though tougher than ordinary crabs, they are still weaker than the massive Megacrabs and tournament-bred specimens. They are mature creatures, fully grown and more dangerous than younger crabs.

Elite Droneguards are the personal guards of the Queen of the South in the Southern Hive territories. They are highly skilled soldier drones, far more capable than standard Droneguards, and protect the Queen directly. They will attack anyone who trespasses into the Queen's domain.

Elite Hunters are the special forces of the United Cities, sent to eliminate high-value targets who have angered the Empire or Trader's Guild. They are highly skilled warriors with excellent equipment and identify themselves by unique names rather than ranks. They typically attack in small groups and are known for their deadly efficiency in combat.

Emperor Anzai was the former ruler of the United Cities before Emperor Tengu. He died in battle during the Red Rebellion, which many believe was secretly orchestrated by Longen of the Traders Guild, possibly with help from the Nobles. His reign and death are mostly remembered through whispers and an unsigned letter called Puppet.

Emperor Tengu is the current leader of the United Cities, ruling from his throne room in Heft alongside his diplomat Koin and a large retinue of elite guards. He is known for being impulsive and lacking common sense compared to his predecessor, and maintains power through fear with his Inner Circle of four cruel nobles. Despite his fearsome reputation and stories of his mysterious Vault where enemies are sent, Tengu is only an average fighter who relies heavily on his bodyguards for protection.
tags: Bosses, Characters, Leaders, Nobles, Unique, United Cities

topic_desc_basic: Endin is a ruined city in Bast controlled by the United Cities. It was largely destroyed by the Holy Army along with the cities of Bast and Drin. The only intact building is a storm house inhabited by harmless vagrants and exiles, with no Samurai guards present.

Esata the Stone Golem is the current leader of the Shek Kingdom, ruling from Admag alongside her daughter Seto and her advisor Bayan. She earned her battle name as one of The Five Invincibles and took power after defeating the previous emperor Shager in combat when she opposed his plan for a suicidal assault on The Holy Nation. Unlike past leaders, Esata seeks to balance the Shek's warrior traditions with strategic thinking to prevent her people from fighting themselves into extinction, though this pragmatic approach has divided her battle-hungry citizens.
tags: Bosses, Bounty, Characters, Leaders, Shek Kingdom, Superbosses, Unique

topic_desc_basic: The Exile Plank is a hefty sword once taken from a defeated Shek Guardian. Without their name, status, or prized weapons, the shamed ones walk the land forever as lost ghosts. It is a type of heavy plank weapon that must be carried in a backpack or equipped, as it does not fit in standard inventories.

Captain-General Eyegore is a hiveless Southern Soldier Drone who leads the United Cities army. He is considered the Empire's ultimate solution to serious problems and will personally lead a final assault against those who have severely angered the United Cities. He wears samurai armor and wields a desert sabre, commanding squads of samurai warriors in his raids.
tags: Bosses, Characters, Hivers, Raiders, Samurai, Superbosses, Traders Guild, Unique, United Cities

topic_desc_basic: Eyesocket is a slave camp located on a small hill in the Stormgap Coast region, run by Slave Master Grande. It supplies nearby settlements and serves as a place where slaves are bought and sold. If Slave Master Grande is killed or taken, the camp falls into ruin and becomes abandoned.

Eyesocket was once a town controlled by the Holy Empire, located in the central regions near Telbooze, Black Scratch, and Skinner's Roam. In later times, the town changed allegiance and became part of the United Cities instead.

The Falling Sun is a ridiculously unwieldy heavy weapon sometimes used by Skeletons, widely known as a 'Suicide Blade' because it often gets its users killed. It requires both dexterity and strength to wield properly, and is the lightest of the heavy weapons. An experienced user is someone to be feared, as the weapon can deal devastating damage in a single strike.
Finch is a Hive Prince who leads the Machinists faction and resides in World's End. Finch refers to Iyo as his assistant and directs visitors to speak with them about historical matters.

Fishman Island is a small zone south of the Bonefields, accessible by a bridge so travelers do not need to swim. The area experiences mad rain with occasional acid rain. It contains ancient ruins and nests but has no permanent settlements or outposts.

Fishmen, also called Gurglers, are fish-like creatures living on Fishman Island south of Catun. They infest the ruins of Fish Isle and are led by King Gurgler, who dwells in the Island Lab. Though individually weak, they attack in large groups and capture injured victims to eat them alive at their nests.

The Five Invincibles are the greatest warriors of the Shek Kingdom, found at their headquarters in Admag. They lead the most important military assaults for the Shek and will join Kral's Chosen if Esata the Stone Golem is killed or imprisoned. They wear specialist-grade armor and carry weapons made by Skeleton Smiths.

The Flat Topper was a hacker-class weapon that mixed cutting and blunt damage, favored by thugs for its reliance on brute force over finesse. It was removed from the world when the map changed, with longswords taking its place. Though no longer found, some say the design still exists somewhere in forgotten records.

Flats Lagoon is a relatively safe zone in the southeastern lands, bordered by Bonefields, Shem, Venge, Stobe's Gamble, and Greyshelf. A land bridge south of the town allows travelers to reach Mourn without swimming.
aliases: Flats Lagoon (Zone), Flats_Lagoon_(Zone), Flats Lagoon Zone

topic_desc_basic: Flats Lagoon Bar is a drinking establishment located in Flats Lagoon. It serves as the regular hangout of Chad, a well-known tech hunter in the region.

Flatskin is a derogatory term used by Shek to describe humans, referring to their lack of horns and the rough bone plates that cover Shek skin. The term reflects the importance of horns in Shek culture and highlights the physical differences between the two races.

The Flesh Cleaver is a crude hacking weapon designed to maim rather than cause bleeding, favored by Cannibals and Shrieking Bandits. Its blunt design makes it effective at cutting and stunning victims through sheer brutality. The weapon is particularly nasty against human targets but less effective against animals.

The Floodlands is a gloomy, flooded swamp caught in endless rain, littered with ancient industrial ruins from a time when machines built more machines in staggering quantities. The land is dead and barren, exploited long ago to feed an insatiable hunger. Only Iron Spiders and Skeletons roam these desolate ruins now.

Flotsam Village is a settlement in the Hidden Forest led by Moll and protected by the Flotsam Ninjas. It shelters refugees and deserters from the Holy Nation, though many residents still worship Okran and distrust skeletons. If Moll dies or is imprisoned, the village falls to Cannibals and becomes overrun.

Flying Bull, also called Ida, is a massive Shek warrior who leads Kral's Chosen from his rebel outpost at New Kralia. He was a devoted follower of the former king Shager and rejected the Stone Golem's leadership, calling her a coward for making peace with the Holy Nation instead of fighting to the end. He carries a unique axe gifted by Shager and is considered an extremist and traitor by the current Shek Kingdom.

Fog Deathyards are camps that appear in the Fog Islands, marked by torch posts, bone-decorated stakes, and prisoner poles. Fogmen bring unconscious victims to these places to worship and devour them, often attracting Fog Princes to feed on captives. If certain faction leaders like The Queen or Phoenix are killed, these deathyards can spread into their former territories.

The Fog Islands are valleys shrouded in perpetual low fog, littered with massive metal scraps from a forgotten civilization. Savage cannibalistic Fogmen, believed to be Hivers who lost their Queen's influence long ago, hunt through the mist to capture and devour travelers. The free city of Mongrel stands as the only safe refuge in this dangerous land, never falling to the Fogmen despite their constant threat.

Fogmen are savage Hivers who inhabit the Fog Islands, having lost their minds to some kind of parasite that controls them from within. They attack anyone who enters their territory, dragging victims back to camps where they are tied to poles and eaten alive by Fog Princes or Fog Heavies. Though individually weak fighters, they travel in large groups and can overwhelm even skilled warriors through sheer numbers.

Foodcubes are dense, nutritious blocks made from a mixture of bread and greenfruit. They are disappointing to eat but practical for travel rations. They can be cooked or purchased from traders throughout the land.

The Forbidden Isle is a small, hostile landmass east of Stormgap Coast, overrun by legions of Iron Spiders emerging from an ancient Spider Factory at its center. Aggressive Tech Hunters also roam the isle, seeking lost secrets amid the ruins. Frequent acid rain blankets the island, making exploration extremely dangerous without proper protection.

Forbidden Sympathy is an illegal book written by an unknown author in the Holy Nation. It argues that all people, regardless of race or status, deserve compassion and that spiritual teachings should progress alongside knowledge and technology. Possession of this book is forbidden in Holy Nation lands and will result in arrest.

The Foreign Sabre is an exotic blade believed to have come from the Black Desert. Despite being mocked in bars and carrying a social stigma, it is actually a defensive masterpiece that should not be underestimated. The finest example of this weapon is carried by the Bugmaster.

Fort Mirage is a small outpost in The Great Desert controlled by Lord Mirage and garrisoned by City Heroes of the United Heroes League. Visitors are attacked on sight, and the fort is defended by mounted crossbow turrets. It serves as a minor stronghold for the faction in the desert wastes.

Fort Simion is an outpost in Sinkuun controlled by the Rebel Farmers, where their leader Boss Simion resides. The settlement is defended by gate guards and garrisons, and roaming squads may attack outsiders who aren't allied with them. In earlier times, Fort Simion was a major town under Holy Empire control.

The Fragment Axe is a massive heavy weapon built like a sword, favored by the Shek for its impressive size and brutal power. It is extremely heavy and difficult to wield, requiring great strength to swing effectively. These axes are commonly found in Shek Kingdom shops, and a legendary Meitou quality can be taken from Esata the Stone Golem or Mukai the Mountain.

The Free City is a settlement in Stobe's Gamble controlled by the Anti-Slavers when Tinfist lives and certain other leaders have fallen. It serves as a small waystation with few inhabitants and basic shops. The settlement appears to be a staging point for Anti-Slaver expansion into the desert regions.

The Free Traders are a small faction that runs farm shops in United Cities towns and operates a single trade caravan led by Harmothoe. They strictly forbid hemp production and related goods like biofuel distilleries, hemp farms, bloodrum, and hashish in their territories. Their caravan travels between towns such as Trader's Edge and Heng.

An Item Furnace is a building used to melt down items into raw iron. Weapons and metal armor can be burned to recover iron based on their weight or coverage. Many crafted items containing iron in their production chain also yield small amounts of raw iron when melted.

Garru are common wild herbivores found across many regions, recognizable by their floppy ears, humped backs, and wrinkly skin. They travel in herds and are often tamed as pack beasts by traders and the Western Hive. Though generally peaceful, they become skittish if approached too closely and will attack if provoked, proving surprisingly tough in combat.

Gatwood the Soft was the legendary founder of modern martial arts who lived hundreds or thousands of years ago, possibly during the Second Empire. He trained Tinfist and was known for never taking a single life despite his mastery. His name suggests he may have been easygoing or carefree, and his teachings still influence martial artists today.

General Hat-12 was the Chief of the Second Empire's police force. He is a skeleton who can be found in Ashland Dome IV, wearing armoured rags and carrying a heavy jitte. He was a member of the Second Empire and still exists in the ruins of that fallen civilization.

General Jang is a Skeleton who leads the Hydraulic Knights of the Second Empire and resides in Ashland Dome III. He is known for fighting pirates and cannibals, who call him 'The Inedible One.' Removing his AI Core or CPU will kill him instantly.
Their products were better than rusted weapons from unknown makers but not as strong as higher-grade manufacturers. The company no longer operates in the current era.
A gi is a simple cloth garment worn on the torso, often paired with gi pants. It can be made at a clothing bench and is a basic piece of attire. A black variant called a ninja gi also exists.

Gi pants are simple white legwear that form part of a traditional gi outfit when worn with the matching top. A black version exists called ninja pants. These pants are commonly associated with martial artists and are notably worn by the wanderer Crumblejon.

Goats are small herbivores with bony faceplates that roam in groups across many regions and are often domesticated by Nomads. They can be hunted for meat and skin, but are tougher fighters than they appear and can surprise inexperienced hunters. Domesticated goats can be purchased from Nomad herders and will eat any type of food. They mature quickly and are relatively fast, though they cannot haul goods like other animals.

Gohan is a filling meal made from rice and vegetables, commonly found in The Swamp where riceweed grows plentifully. It provides good nutrition and is often sold cheaply in swamper settlements. Unlike other cooked foods, it can be prepared without needing water for cooking.

Gorillo Bandits are unarmed members of The Gorrillo Bandits who roam the Bonefields and Flats Lagoon, harassing settlements and travelers. They are easily recognized by their unnaturally bulky arms and hunchbacked posture, and wear very little armor. Some are wanted by the United Cities and Shek Kingdom for their crimes.

Gorillos are wild animals found in various regions including Greyshelf, Sniper Valley, Sonorous Dark, Stobe's Gamble, Stobe's Garden, and The Crags. Black gorillos are the most common variety, while Great White Gorillos and War Gorillos are separate from the typical gorillo groups.

Gorrillo is an unusually large and dim-witted bandit leader wanted for robbery, assault, and destruction of property in the lost town of Mourn. He leads the Gorrillo Bandits and hides out in the Old Prison somewhere in the Forbidden Zone. His bounty can be claimed in the Shek Kingdom or United Cities, with Catun being the nearest collection point.

The Grand Fish is considered the king of the two known fish species in the world. It can be found in swampy regions and fishing villages. Unlike the smaller Thinfish, Grand Fish cannot be dried for preservation.

The Grass Pirates are a bandit faction that operates around The Eye and Stormgap Coast, constantly fighting with the United Cities over territory. They are hostile to travelers and can be recognized by their worn sleeveless dustcoats. Unlike most bandits, they are notably skilled in hand-to-hand combat.

Grayflayer Village is a settlement deep in the Swamp, controlled by the Swampers but truly run by the Grayflayers under their leader Big Gray. The Grayflayer headquarters is located here. Travelers can find it by exploring the swamp or by reading a Map of the Swamps.

The Grayflayers are one of five gangs operating in The Swamp, led by Big Gray. They control the city of Shark and Grayflayer Village, dealing primarily in hashish like the other swamp gangs. Their smugglers are commonly seen at the Smugglers Bar and in Grey Desert, though they are considered one of the smaller gangs compared to groups like the Hounds and Blackshifters.
tags: Factions, Grayflayers, Swamp Gangs, Swampers, Swamps

topic_desc_basic: The Great White Gorillo is a massive and exceptionally dangerous variant of the common gorillo, locked away in a laboratory building in the center of Mourn. It is far stronger and faster than ordinary gorillos, and killing it is considered a notable feat-so much so that bringing one of its claws to a bar will earn congratulations and free drinks. Its blood is a deep red, and it is known to be quite old and formidable.

Greenbeach is a coastal zone controlled by the Crab Raiders, who sometimes clash with Reavers. The area is known for its large population of crabs and occasional sightings of beak things. It borders The Outlands, Stobe's Garden, and The Pits East, but has no major towns or ancient ruins.

Greenfruit is a vegetable used as a cooking ingredient, despite its misleading name. It cannot be eaten raw and must be processed at a cooking stove or turned into biofuel. It is grown on farms and can be purchased from trade goods traders or certain vendors.

Greenlanders are the most common type of human found throughout the world, especially in the Holy Nation territories. They have no particular strengths or weaknesses, making them adaptable to any role or environment. Unlike some other races, they require standard protective gear when traveling through harsh weather conditions.

The Grey Desert is a small, mostly empty zone bordered by some of the most polluted lands in the world, including the Deadlands, Venge, and the Black Desert. A single Tech Hunter waystation serves as the last resupply point before travelers head deeper into the wastes. Wandering groups of traders, nomads, bloodraiders, and occasional thralls from Venge pass through the area.

Greyshelf is a highland zone in the southeast, separated from Royal Valley by mountains and bordering the Southern Hive's heartlands. The area is known for its gorillo populations and old armories, some claimed by the Southern Hive. Travelers should beware of acid rain that sometimes falls in this region.

Grog is a traditional weak alcoholic drink made from wheatstraw and water. It's brewed in grog machines and stored in special barrels. Despite being alcohol, even skeletons are known to drink it in their bars and settlements.

Gurglers are the most common type of Fishmen found roaming in large packs on Fishman Island, south of the Bonefields. They are not particularly skilled fighters but rely on overwhelming numbers to take down enemies. Like other Fishmen, they fight using their claws in unarmed combat.
Gurgler eggs are creepy fishman eggs stolen from gurgler nests found on Fishman Island. These large eggs come from the gurglers, one of the fishman breeds that inhabit the dangerous coastal regions.

Gut is a dangerous region east of the desert known for its distinctive sky-blue sands and scattered iron trees. The area is infested with beak things, making travel extremely hazardous, though the creatures provide valuable resources for those brave enough to hunt them. The zone takes its name from the gutters that inhabit the area, and it lacks any major settlements or ancient ruins.

The Gutters are a faction consisting entirely of Beak Things, dangerous predatory creatures found primarily in Gut and scattered across many harsh regions of the world. These beasts roam in squads and establish nests in desolate areas like the Bonefields, Cannibal Plains, and Venge. They are wild animals rather than an organized group, posing a deadly threat to travelers in their territories.

Harpoon Turrets are defensive installations used to guard outposts and buildings. They can be mounted on walls or placed freely, and their effectiveness depends on the operator's skill and the height advantage over targets. An upgraded version exists that can be fitted with a spotlight for nighttime defense.

Hashish is a narcotic drug made from hemp that is illegal in most towns throughout the world. Getting caught smuggling it can lead to arrest, but it remains popular in borderland areas where laws are less strictly enforced. It can be purchased in Hive Villages and The Swamp, or produced by processing hemp in illegal structures that may attract unwanted attention from authorities.

The Head of Agriculture is a Skeleton who once served the Second Empire. They now reside in Ashland Dome I, surrounded by Legion Thralls. This ancient figure carries a legendary short cleaver and possesses a unique CPU core from their former role.

Heft is the capital of the United Cities, located in the Great Desert. It is home to Emperor Tengu, the leader of the United Cities, along with Lord Ohta and the diplomat Koin. The town features notable shops including an armory with high-quality armor, a thieves guild, and a robotics workshop.

Heft was an old town that sat on a cliff in the southeast, marked by a large metal cage at its center. It was once controlled by Dead Cat and located near Bark and Black Scratch. The town eventually became a major city in the United Cities.

Heft Armory is an armour shop run by the Tech Hunters in the town of Heft. The shop stocks various protective gear and restocks its inventory regularly. Its presence may change depending on events in the world.

Heft Armory is an armor shop run by the Tech Hunters in the town of Heft. The shop stocks various protective gear and restocks its inventory regularly. Its presence may change depending on events in the world.

Hemp is a raw material grown on farms that is commonly used to make fabrics and clothing. It can also be processed into fuel or medical items. The United Cities consider it illegal because it can be turned into hashish, though other factions do not outlaw hemp itself.

Heng is a major United Cities settlement built on a rocky plateau, connected by a metal bridge to its satellite city, Trader's Edge, which houses the Traders Guild headquarters. It serves as the Empire's main trading hub and is heavily defended, with Lord Yoshinaga residing in the Noble House under guard. The town is supported by several slave camps and features a Thieves Guild and a Robotics Workshop for repairs.

Heng is the heartland of the United Cities and home to the Traders Guild, centered around a major city of the same name. The zone is crowded with slave caravans, merchant convoys, mercenaries, bounty hunters, and manhunters all seeking profit, as well as escaped slaves and rebels trying to survive. It is a dangerous land of opportunity where fortunes can be made or lost, and strangers are often targeted by opportunists on all sides. The region experiences great desert conditions and borders zones like Howler Maze, Gut, The Eye, Skimsands, and The Great Desert.

Hidden Forest is a sparse, rocky forested region known as the hideout of the Flotsam Ninjas. The area is infested with Cannibals and dangerous creatures, with locals whispering that it lies near the mouth of the abyss where demons and unholy monsters emerge. The northern areas near the coast have better water and soil, while the south is mostly barren rock.

The High Bonefields is a mountain range located north of Catun. It is a barren, uninhabited region with no settlements or ancient ruins. The area experiences dry boneyard conditions and is known for its desolate terrain.

High Inquisitor Seta is a high-ranking member of the Holy Nation's Inquisition and serves as part of the Holy Lord Phoenix's command. He governs the southern cities of Stack and Bad Teeth and commands the forces defending against the Shek Kingdom along the southern border. His death or capture severely weakens the Holy Nation's southern front and can trigger major shifts in territorial control across multiple regions.
tags: Bosses, Bounty, Characters, Holy Nation, Inquisitors, Superbosses, Unique

topic_desc_basic: High Inquisitor Valtena is a powerful commander of the Holy Nation's Inquisition, stationed at Okran's Shield and leading the northern and eastern military campaigns against the United Cities in Bast and Skimsands. He commands vast forces and can personally lead the Wrath of God event against enemies of the Holy Nation. His death would trigger the collapse of the northeastern front, causing widespread chaos and shifts in territorial control across multiple regions.
tags: Bosses, Bounty, Characters, Holy Nation, Inquisitors, Superbosses, Unique

topic_desc_basic: High Overseers are the commanding authority figures who run the Holy Nation's mines. They oversee daily operations, keep the Lower Servants in line, and command the garrison of Slavers, Paladins, and Holy Sentinels stationed at the mine. They dress similarly to High Paladins but do not wear helmets or carry a Paladin's Cross. Killing a High Overseer does not shut down the mine itself.

High Paladins are elite squad leaders and bodyguards in the Holy Nation army, often commanding patrols of Paladins and Holy Servants. They hold senior rank and do not answer to the priestly caste, though they report to their own commanders and inquisitors. High Paladins enforce Holy Nation law in their lands, sometimes giving aid to human men but demanding non-humans surrender as slaves or face hostility.

Hivers are stick-like humanoids who live under collective hive minds ruled by queens and princes, hatching from eggs through the queen's parthenogenesis. When separated from their hive too long, they lose their mental bond and become Hiveless, gaining free will but feeling purposeless and often seeking new masters or turning to crime. The two main hives are the Western Hive, which is large and trades peacefully with outsiders, and the smaller, violent Southern Hive in the southeast. Hivers completely cut off from their queen can become corrupted into insane, cannibalistic Fogmen.

Hive Bandits are members of the Western Hive who turn to banditry after their Hive Queen is killed or kidnapped. They roam in small groups led by a Hive Bandit Leader across western and some eastern regions. They wear ragged armor and carry bladed weapons or polearms.

Hive Princes are a rare subrace of Western Hivers who evolved to be more independent and can remain separated from the main Hive for long periods. They are the most intelligent of all Hiver breeds and do not eat Foul Raw Meat like other Hivers. Free Princes are uncommon because of their independent nature, though versions exist among the Dead Hive and Southern Hive as well.

Hive Queens are the rare rulers of the Hiver race, distinguished by their six antennae and the metal dispenser units fused to their bodies. Only two are known to exist: the Queen of the West and the Queen of the South. Despite their organic appearance, their bodies are partly mechanical and cannot be healed with ordinary bandages.

Hive Villages are settlements of the Western Hive found in the regions of Vain and Dreg. They are inhabited by worker drones who labor and flee from danger, soldier drones who guard the village with polearms, and hive princes who act as traders. The villagers refuse to trade with hiveless individuals, and if the Queen dies, these villages fall to Fogmen or potentially Slave Traders.

Hive Worker Drones are a subrace of the Western Hive, known for their skills in thievery and building. They have weaker limbs that are prone to injury, often requiring replacement with robotic parts. They are immune to certain weather conditions and have restrictions on what equipment they can wear.

Holy Citizens are Greenlander residents of Holy Nation cities and the free populace alongside farmers. They rank above the slave castes and react with surprise to seeing unshackled Shek or other non-humans. They typically purchase rice bowls and cactus rum for their daily needs.

The Holy Edict is a decree from Holy Lord Phoenix LXII condemning foreign women for wearing jewelry made of gold, silver, and iron. It declares that such materials should be used for tools to maintain order, not for vanity, and orders that any woman wearing jewelry without a guardian be flogged until she repents. The edict reflects the Holy Nation's strict religious laws and their hostility toward outsiders, particularly those from more luxurious societies.

Holy Farms are scattered agricultural settlements throughout Holy Nation territory that supply food for the faction. They are worked by Holy Farmers and their wives, growing crops like wheat, greenfruit, cotton, and occasionally cactus. If Phoenix dies and Esata lives, the farmers complain about Shek raiders demanding tribute, though the farms remain under Holy Nation control.

Holy Farm Leaders are Greenlander men who run Holy Farms in Holy Nation territory. They wear turbans and white vests and carry iron clubs. Unlike most Holy Nation traders, they will trade with non-humans as long as they have no robotic limbs, selling domesticated animals like bulls and dogs along with farm goods.

The Holy Flame is the religious book of the Holy Nation, and every citizen is required by law to own one. Carrying it can help avoid trouble with Paladins and Inquisitors, and it is necessary for observing Prayer Day. The book is commonly found throughout Holy Nation territory.

Holy Lord Phoenix is the 62nd reincarnation of the Lawgiver and supreme leader of the Holy Nation, ruling from his throne room in Blister Hill surrounded by High Paladins and his bodyguard. Raised in isolation and indoctrinated from childhood, he sentenced his own family to death at age sixteen and has dedicated his life to eradicating the Shek Kingdom. His death causes mass panic and chaos throughout the Holy Nation, potentially leading to the collapse of Blister Hill itself.
tags: Bosses, Bounty, Characters, Holy Nation, Superbosses, Unique

topic_desc_basic: Holy Mines are mining outposts scattered across Holy Nation territory where slaves and captured enemies are forced to work under the watch of overseers and guards. Lower Servants and bandits are caged at night and sent to labor during the day. These sites are guarded by Holy Sentinels and Paladins, with additional slavers sometimes present to help manage the operations.

The Holy Nation is a large democratic farming society guided by the faith of Christianism, centered around Christian's Pride and led by an elected figurehead called the Phoenix. They claim to value freedom, equality, and moral governance, welcoming all visitors and resolving conflicts through peaceful means. The nation has faced repeated raids and border wars but maintains its territory through citizen militias and careful diplomacy. Their records are among the oldest on the continent, dating back to the fall of the First Empire.

Holy Priests are high-ranking religious figures of the Holy Nation who devote themselves to the god Okran and typically remain near temples. They lead prayer ceremonies and may lecture female characters or call Paladins to deal with non-human races they view as threats. Freeing a Holy Priest from slavery earns favor with the Holy Nation.

The Holy Seal is a blessed token given by the Holy Lord Phoenix to those who pledge to destroy his enemies and maintain good standing with the Holy Nation. It can be shown to paladins for aid and assistance. The seal is a mark of favor from the Phoenix himself and carries significant value as a holy relic.

The Horse Chopper is a classic sabre with a heavy, curved blade designed for cutting and defending. It's very common across the wasteland and often wielded by Dust Bandits, Red Sabres, and other bandit groups.

The Hounds are the most powerful gang in The Swamp and the main growers of hemp, which is used to make hashish, a narcotic illegal in the major nations. Their leader Big Grim is known for being both crazy and clever enough to control the swamp hierarchy. They operate out of Shark and the village of Rot, and will offer protection to those who build bases in The Swamp in exchange for payment or loyalty.

The Howler Maze is an uninhabited island connected to the mainland by land bridges, located between Heng and Gut. It is dominated by crabs and scattered with ancient ruins, with occasional escaped slaves wandering through from nearby UC territory. The island experiences acid rain and features what appears to be a crater or old volcano caldera on its southern side.

Humans are the most common race in the world, divided into Greenlanders and Scorchlanders. Greenlanders resemble typical humans with balanced abilities, while Scorchlanders have darker skin, glowing eyes, and silvery hair with natural talent in crafting and agility. Humanity's origins stretch back to an ancient, technologically advanced First Empire, though most people today know little of their own history.

Hundred Guardians are the elite soldiers of the Shek Kingdom, representing the top one hundred fighters in their society. They patrol the lands, guard major cities like Admag and Squin, and serve as law enforcement within Shek territory. These warriors are neutral but disdainful toward humans, calling them flatskins, and will attack those allied with the Holy Nation. If allied with the Shek Kingdom, wandering Hundred Guardians can be hired temporarily as bodyguards or outpost guards.

Hydraulic Knights are skeletal warriors from the Second Empire who guard Ashland Dome III. They wear ancient samurai armor and carry nodachi blades forged by skilled skeleton smiths. Five of these mechanical sentinels remain in the dome, standing as remnants of a long-fallen empire.

Hydroponics are advanced indoor farming structures that allow crops to grow anywhere, regardless of the local environment or soil quality. They require water and electrical power to function, and can cultivate greenfruit, hemp, riceweed, and wheatstraw even in barren or toxic zones. These farms are built with iron plates, electrical components, and seeds of the crop to be grown.

Idad was an author who wrote several books about ancient history, legends, and cultural evolution. Based on the scholarly nature of these works, Idad was likely a Machinist. Idad's current whereabouts or fate remain unknown.

Inquisitors are elite law enforcers and commanding generals of the Holy Nation who run the Inquisitoriums and lead the Holy Army. They seek out heretics of Okran, oversee town police stations, handle prisoners and confiscated goods, and command patrols of Paladins. Inquisitors are powerful warriors who rank among the highest in the Holy Nation, with High Inquisitors serving directly under the Holy Phoenix. They only deal with human males and are dismissive of women and non-humans.

Iron HQ is an outpost in The Crags that serves as the headquarters of the Skeleton Bandits, led by Elder. The settlement consists of wallhouses and a central lab where Elder resides. Skeleton visitors have an easier time negotiating with Elder than humans, as the bandits are generally hostile to non-skeletons.

Iron Spiders are old robotic creatures that roam regions like the Floodlands, Deadlands, and The Iron Trail.
